Where click optimisation moves the click

Prompt tokens of real and optimised clicks in Medical-SAM3's geometry encoder · paper supplement S3.3 (“What optimising the click changes”)

CMAS optimises the click's prompt tokens before it records the activation differences. For each slice, we embed 20 positive clicks at random pixels inside the ground-truth mask and 20 negative clicks on a ring 3–8 px outside it (fewer on very small structures). The random initial click (○) is one of the positive clicks; the line runs to the optimised click (◆). The real positive and negative clicks are perfectly linearly separable, and about 98% of the gap between them is the click label (positive vs. negative), not its location. The optimised clicks stay on the positive side but move far off the cloud of real clicks, mostly perpendicular to the positive–negative axis. Diagnostic on the middle slice of every class in the first five test volumes of each dataset (RAOS 89, ToothFairy2 66 slices); it uses test data for analysis only and is not used to select or tune the method.
Hover a point for its class, slice, distance to the nearest real positive click and Dice.

Axes are true Euclidean components in token space (same units as the paper), not t-SNE. Per-slice axes (the paper's): x = the slice's positive–negative axis (unit vector from the negative to the positive centroid), y = the direction of that slice's displacement perpendicular to x (so the initial → optimised line lies exactly in the x–y plane at its true length), z = the main direction of the slice's real clicks orthogonal to both; origin = midpoint of the slice's two centroids, and all slices are overlaid in their own frames (× = centroids). Pooled: x = the dataset's pooled positive–negative axis, y/z = the top-2 principal directions of all displacements perpendicular to it. Distances between points that are not along these axes are lower bounds of the full distances; the hover values and the readout are computed in the full token space. Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom.

Research use only. Data: RAOS and ToothFairy2 test volumes (see the project page for credits).
